I never went to school. I learned to farm from my mother and father starting when I was very small. Now I am 37 and I take care of our 10.1 mu in Quzhou. Some of my family works in the factory in the city, but I stay here to grow wheat and maize.

The wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu when I sowed it. Now spring is here, and I will spread half a bag — about 20 jin — of urea on every mu when the wheat starts turning green. If some spots look yellow, I put a little extra there. My neighbor Lao Wang puts a full half-bag on each mu and his wheat is always tall and dark, so I do the same. I am not afraid of using too much — if I use too little and the yield is bad, my family suffers. A few extra yuan on fertilizer is nothing compared to a bad harvest.

I water the wheat three times: once now if the winter was dry, once when the stems start growing fast, and once when the grain is getting plump. I spray medicine twice — once to kill the weeds, and once when the bugs show up in late spring. Before I planted the wheat, I used the rotary machine to turn the soil.

In June, after cutting the wheat, I plant maize the same day on all 10.1 mu. I buy hybrid seed from the shop — the old kinds don't grow enough anymore. I put compound fertilizer in the rows when I plant, about one 40-jin bag per mu, and then when the maize is about knee-high, I spread another 20 jin of urea per mu. I water twice in summer if the rain doesn't come, and spray twice — once for weeds and once for the worms that eat corn. After the wheat comes off, I use the rotary tiller to prepare the ground.

Last year my wheat gave about 550 kg per mu and the maize gave about 600 kg per mu. That was enough to cover the fertilizer and seed money and leave some for the family. So this year I will do exactly the same. I don't try new things. Two years ago, a man in the next village tried a new way and his crop failed. I cannot take that risk.
